_doc: Confidence scored lessons. Top 5 with confidence at or above 0.7 are injected into every subagent prompt. Bump 0.05 per confirming run, drop 0.1 per contradicting run, prune below 0.5 when older than 8 runs.

instincts.instinct: Fit display headlines with AK.fitText inside renderReady instead of hand tuned font sizes. Hand sized hooks wrap an extra line and collide with the block below.
instincts.evidence: Engine proof slide-01 failed QA exactly this way before fitText max was tightened. Same recurring defect class in the sibling studio through 2026-07-09.

instincts.instinct: Give every absolutely positioned text block an explicit vertical budget. A bottom anchored block under a top anchored stack collides the moment content grows a line.
instincts.evidence: Engine proof slide-02 stats stack collided with the bottom honesty note until row padding and font were budgeted.

instincts.instinct: Constellation micro text (site line, coordinates) must carry data-decorative or QA flags it as tiny text.
instincts.evidence: Engine proof slide-03 warned on the 21px site line until marked.

instincts.instinct: Lead case posts with the ordinary company detail (size, founding year, family ownership) before the technology. The reader must think, that is basically us, before they will care how it works.
instincts.evidence: Hypothesis from the evidence base (identification precedes persuasion in the MIT winner profile and the ICP). Unconfirmed by post metrics yet.

instincts.instinct: Vendor sourced numbers get the label in the same breath as the number, never in a footnote. Trust is the product this series sells.
instincts.evidence: House law restated as craft. Run 1 confirmed, the case-critic caught an unlabeled caption number and a mis-classed chip.

instincts.instinct: DOM chips and labels placed in the art zone must be checked against canvas data mark coordinates at plan time. Machine QA cannot see canvas, so these collisions survive to the pixel critics or to the reader.
instincts.evidence: Run 1 had two instances, the S3 chip row covered dashed series nodes and the S5 footer wrapped into the canvas cost stair.

instincts.instinct: The caption must never claim more than the most hedged slide supports. Write the hook FROM the verified claim text, not from the story's vibe.
instincts.evidence: Run 1's hook said one technician tallies every fish all season, c23 supports a technician counting fish images on video. The case-critic caught it, the fix was a near restatement of the state's own page.

instincts.instinct: Plant the next slide on any keepable slide. A save worthy scoreboard invites exit, one forward tease line at the predicted bail point makes saving and swiping the same impulse.
instincts.evidence: Flow critic named S5 the bail point for exactly this reason on run 1, the tease was the fix.

instincts.instinct: Hunt where the money is public. Award submissions, vendor blogs and trade press are written to win something, and cost is the one number that never helps you win. Public safety, utilities, school districts and municipal services publish contract values because the money is a public surcharge.
instincts.evidence: Restock wave 1 returned zero banks across four private-sector grounds, fourteen candidates, every one failing the cost hard gate. Wave 2 opened the public-safety vein and produced the run's only qualifying case with both figures on the record.

instincts.instinct: Solve an honesty problem compositionally, not in captions. Two numbers that share no base must be separated on four axes at once: different slide, different glyph species, different geometry, different ground, with the base printed on the rule that measures it.
instincts.evidence: Slide 6 carries the 41,000 and the annual 105,000 lives on slide 2. When the baseline rule and the bar shared a left origin the pixel critic read the 2024 baseline as SMALLER than seven months of calls, which inverts the truth. Separating the origins fixed a misread that no caption could have.

instincts.instinct: Never let a rule cross a number. On the slide whose job is handing the reader a figure to carry to their CFO, a mis-placed sum rule made both dollar totals read as struck through, which says voided.
instincts.evidence: Slide 8 shipped a scotch rule at the total's mid x-height for a full render pass and four machine gates without a single gate catching it. Only the pixel critic saw it. Machine gates check collisions between TEXT nodes and declared ART rects; a canvas rule inside a declared art rect crossing a knockout label is invisible to them.

instincts.instinct: Never hand-type a reader-facing string at a tool call. If the copy record holds it, read it from the copy record. Corrections that land in copy.json do not propagate to anything a human types by hand.
instincts.evidence: copy.json carried a slide_copy_corrections entry that had already replaced an em-dashed document title, and the showrunner then typed an em-dashed title straight into the assemble.py --title flag. It shipped into the PDF metadata, which LinkedIn renders under the carousel, and cost the run its only hard fail and 0.24 of score.
